Q: English language does not listed in App Store page A:

If you're like me, using String Catalog in SwiftUI, and expected that if you see the same values for the key and English (en) (or your base language) columns, it should automatically use those values for localization, you are probably in the same trap.

To resolve the issue, just copy/paste values from the key column or fill in all of the missing English (en) column values and submit a new build to the TestFlight. Once it's uploaded, you may easily verify it by going to the Build Metadata.

Sign in to the App Store Connect -> TestFlight -> Click on build number -> Build Metadata (tab) -> Scroll down and check Localizations. Make sure you can see your base language there before submitting the app to the review in order for the language to appear.

Thanks to the author for this post, took me some time to figure it out.

P.S: And yeah, don't expect for Xcode 26.3 to show you any checkmarks for the base language.

Q: Source generation: working with attributes with arguments of type System.Type A:

You cannot get a hold of the System.Type instance as you expect.

Roslyn operates at compile time. None of the code you are analyzing is loaded into memory by the CLR and is actually being executed. Therefore, the runtime concept of System.Type doesn't exist. (Yes, it exists for the execution context of the Roslyn Generator, but that is not useful for achieving your goals).

You should just access the attribute argument as an ITypeSymbol (or whatever ISymbol instance you prefer) and perform any computations from there. Roslyn provides these semantic symbols for this reason.
